answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the ember check immediately, the zenith audit keeps the resolved set and the bridge replay makes public exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 89 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 89 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
